references.text: Describes the detailed regulation for the showbread: twelve loaves that were to be arranged in two rows on a table of pure gold, with incense, as a perpetual covenant offering to the Lord.
Mentions the table and its poles and all its utensils, along with the showbread, as part of the tabernacle equipment.
Describes Bezalel's construction of the acacia wood table on which the showbread was to be placed, including all its utensils.
Moses set the table in the tent of meeting and arranged the bread before the Lord, just as the Lord had commanded.
Instruction to cover the table of showbread with a blue cloth when the camp was to break camp, noting that the bread was to remain there continually.
David received holy bread (the showbread) from the priest Ahimelech at Nob while fleeing from Saul.
Solomon made the gold table on which the showbread was placed in the temple.
Mentions the tables for the showbread among the furnishings of the temple.
Describes how the Levites place the showbread on the clean table every Sabbath as part of proper worship.
The people commit to providing the showbread as part of the service in God's house.
Jesus refers to the time David ate the showbread, which only priests were allowed to eat, during his discussion about the Sabbath.
Jesus notes that David entered God's house and ate the showbread when he was hungry.
Luke's account of Jesus referring to David eating the showbread.
Describes the first tabernacle with its lampstand and table and the showbread, called the Holy Place.
Both verses establish the principle of continuous service ('always'/'every day') carried out directly 'before God's face'.
Both verses define 'constant' presence (bread and offering) as an expression of God's eternal presence at the tent of meeting.
